value.body: An optometrist tests vision, checks the eyes for common problems, and prescribes and fits glasses and contact lenses. Employers include eye hospitals, ophthalmology clinics, optical retail stores and lens manufacturers. A day is mostly patient examinations: refraction, basic eye-health checks, lens fitting and referring patients to an ophthalmologist when needed.

items.label: Regulation
items.value: National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021
items.note: Optometry is listed as an allied health profession

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Retinoscope, autorefractor, slit lamp, trial lens set

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology (some colleges also accept Mathematics), then a B.Optom or B.Sc Optometry. After the internship, freshers usually start as optometrists in eye hospitals, clinics or optical stores.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Using a slit lamp and other eye-testing equipment
Fitting and following up contact lenses
Screening for conditions that need referral
Explaining eye care to patients clearly

value.title: At a glance
items: Specialisations include contact lenses, low vision, paediatric optometry and binocular vision.
Some optometrists open their own optical practice after a few years.
Surgery and most medical treatment are outside the role; those patients are referred to an ophthalmologist.
